subject: math

objective.text: Find totals for equal groups using repeated addition and multiplication. Explain what the number of groups and the number in each group mean, and combine two sets of equal groups.

explanations.title: Equal groups
explanations.text: Equal groups have the same number of objects in every group. Three bags with 4 apples in each bag are 3 equal groups of 4.

explanations.title: Add equal groups
explanations.text: To find the total, add the number in each group once for every group. Three bags with 4 apples each give 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 apples.

explanations.title: Multiply equal groups
explanations.text: In this lesson, number of groups times number in each group gives the total. Three bags with 4 apples each are written as 3 times 4 equals 12. The 3 counts the bags, the 4 counts the apples in each bag, and the 12 counts all the apples.

explanations.title: Combine two sets of groups
explanations.text: Find the total for each set, then add those totals. Two bags with 4 apples each give 8 apples. Three more bags with 4 apples each give 12 apples. Altogether, 8 + 12 = 20 apples. You can also combine the 5 bags and calculate 5 times 4 equals 20.

explanations.title: Empty groups
explanations.text: An empty box contains 0 objects. Four empty boxes contain 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 objects. Four times 0 equals 0.

examples.title: Three bags of four apples
examples.text: There are 3 bags with 4 apples in each bag. Repeated addition: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Multiplication: 3 times 4 equals 12. There are 12 apples in total.

examples.title: Two sets of bags
examples.text: There are 2 bags with 4 apples each and 3 more bags with 4 apples each. First set: 2 times 4 equals 8. Second set: 3 times 4 equals 12. Combined total: 8 + 12 = 20 apples.

questions.text: There are 3 boxes with 2 crayons in each box. How many crayons are there altogether?
There are 5 bowls with 4 apples in each bowl. How many apples are there altogether?

The first set has 4 packets with 3 stickers in each packet. The second set has 2 packets with 3 stickers in each packet. How many stickers are in the first set, in the second set, and altogether? Give all three answers.
There are 3 bags with 4 apples in each bag. We write 3 times 4 equals 12. What does the 3 mean, what does the 4 mean, and what does the 12 mean?
There are 4 empty boxes. Each box contains 0 crayons. How many crayons are there altogether?

hints.text: Add the number in one group once for each group.
Multiply the number of groups by the number in each group.
Find the total in the first set. Then find the total in the second set.
Add the two totals to find how many objects there are altogether.
Which number tells you how many bags there are? Which tells you how many apples are in each bag?
Each box is empty. How many objects are in an empty box?

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
